core_gameplay_loop: Explore; settle; improve districts; research; negotiate or fight; pursue victory
player_goal: Achieve one of several civilization victories
economy_resources: Food; production; gold; science; culture; strategic resources
army: Tile units; combined support; promotions
combat: Deterministic tactical tile combat
technology_progression: Technology and civic trees with activity-based boosts
strengths: Clear long arc; several viable victory vectors; geography shapes cities
player_friction: Late-game turn load and system stacking can dilute individual decisions
lesson_for_our_game: Let terrain alter city specialization and offer visible medium-term goals; cap slice length

core_gameplay_loop: Gather; build; age up; produce army; scout; attack
player_goal: Destroy or outscore rivals; complete campaign objectives
economy_resources: Food; wood; gold; stone; population
army: Readable counters and civilization-specific rosters
world_map: Match map with fog, resources and control points
combat: Real-time micro plus formation and siege decisions
strengths: Strong economy-to-army causality; readable counterplay
player_friction: High APM and early build-order knowledge create an onboarding wall
lesson_for_our_game: Keep economy-to-unit conversion legible; use tactical pause or command cadence for the slice

core_gameplay_loop: Manage empire and armies on campaign map; resolve battles; expand
player_goal: Dominate campaign objectives and rival factions
economy_resources: Treasury; province income; faction resources
army: Large roster armies led by characters
combat: Large real-time field and siege battles
strengths: Powerful campaign-to-battle spectacle; faction asymmetry
player_friction: Long campaigns; autoresolve tension; DLC/content complexity; multiplayer desync reports
lesson_for_our_game: Prototype the campaign/battle handoff with few units before attempting scale or many factions

core_gameplay_loop: Manage ruler; relationships; realm; schemes and wars; handle succession
player_goal: Build a lasting dynasty and personal legacy
city_base: Holdings and domain upgrades rather than free placement
economy_resources: Gold; prestige; piety; levies; opinion
army: Levies; men-at-arms; knights
combat: Campaign-level army movement and resolved battles
technology_progression: Culture; innovations; lifestyle perks; dynasty legacies
monetization: Premium plus expansions and flavor packs
strengths: Emergent character stories make setbacks memorable
player_friction: Dense UI and indirect control can obscure why outcomes occur
lesson_for_our_game: Attach human consequences and named leaders to strategic losses without simulating a full dynasty

core_gameplay_loop: Explore; claim; colonize; specialize; research; diplomatically compete or wage war
player_goal: Shape and secure a customizable interstellar empire
economy_resources: Energy; minerals; food; alloys; consumer goods; research; influence
army: Designed fleets with composition and logistics
combat: Fleet positioning and largely automated battles
strengths: Discovery, customization and emergent crises sustain replay
player_friction: Mid/late-game management load and content layering can overwhelm
lesson_for_our_game: Make scouting produce consequential choices and reserve crises for a compact climax

core_gameplay_loop: Settle; satisfy population tiers; build production chains; trade; expand regions
player_goal: Create a prosperous multi-region industrial network
economy_resources: Multi-stage goods; workforce tiers; ships and trade routes
army: Ships and limited land/naval military elements
combat: Real-time naval and strategic combat
strengths: Deep, visible supply chains and satisfying specialization
player_friction: Logistics scale becomes busywork; combat is secondary for war-focused players
lesson_for_our_game: Use only 3-4 meaningful chains and show physical delivery; automate mature routes

core_gameplay_loop: Gather; heat; build; assign labor; pass laws; survive escalating crises
player_goal: Keep the last city alive without losing social control
city_base: Radial city organized around a heat source
economy_resources: Coal; wood; steel; food; steam cores; labor; heat
army: No conventional army; scouts and guards serve strategic roles
combat: Crisis and policy conflict rather than tactical warfare
strengths: Resources, ethics and time pressure reinforce one fantasy
player_friction: Punishing failure and scripted scenario knowledge reduce relaxed replay
lesson_for_our_game: Tie every resource choice to visible people and consequences; let the slice end with one authored crisis

core_gameplay_loop: Establish settlement; adapt to random blueprints; fulfill orders; leave before hostility wins
player_goal: Complete settlements that advance a persistent campaign
economy_resources: Food and crafting chains; trade; resolve; impatience; hostility
army: No conventional army
combat: Environmental threats and event choices
technology_progression: Run unlocks plus Smoldering City meta-progression
strengths: Short sessions solve city-builder late-game fatigue; forced adaptation boosts replay
player_friction: Players wanting permanent cities may dislike resets; many recipes can overload
lesson_for_our_game: Design a 45-60 minute regional objective with persistent unlocks, not an endless first slice

core_gameplay_loop: Grow village; balance production and trade; claim regions; muster and fight
player_goal: Build a viable domain and contest territory
economy_resources: Physical goods; local labor; trade; seasonal food
army: Militia drawn from population; mercenaries; equipment matters
combat: Real-time formations; fatigue; weather and equipment
multiplayer: Planned/not core in current early-access positioning
strengths: City and army share population and equipment, making losses meaningful
player_friction: Early-access repetition and tension between city-builder and warfare audiences
lesson_for_our_game: Make soldiers remain citizens and keep city/war goals mutually reinforcing

core_gameplay_loop: Claim zones; assign villagers; survive seasons; specialize clan; pursue victory
player_goal: Win through conquest or alternative clan/map objectives
economy_resources: Food; wood; crowns; lore; stone; iron; happiness
army: Small warbands and clan-specific units
world_map: Region graph with hazards and resources
combat: Real-time zone control with low-to-medium micro
technology_progression: Lore tree; building upgrades; clan bonuses
monetization: Premium plus clan DLC; mobile premium
strengths: Scarcity, winter and zone caps keep decisions sharp
player_friction: Resource pressure and clan knowledge can punish newcomers
lesson_for_our_game: Use region capacity and seasonal forecasting to bound city complexity

core_gameplay_loop: Expand economy; clear infected; wall choke points; survive timed hordes
player_goal: Keep colony command center alive
city_base: Defensive colony with power grid and walls
economy_resources: Workers; food; energy; gold; wood; stone; iron; oil
army: Specialized troops, towers and patrols
world_map: Single survival map or campaign nodes
combat: Real-time with pause; high-stakes breach cascades
technology_progression: Building tiers; unit unlocks; campaign research
strengths: Clear build-up/payoff rhythm and spectacular threat escalation
player_friction: One small mistake can cause total cascade; repetition and trial knowledge
lesson_for_our_game: Use a telegraphed final assault and forgiving recovery states for the first slice

core_gameplay_loop: Build settlement; satisfy populations; scale industry; trade; raise armies; conquer
player_goal: Grow from small settlement to regional empire
city_base: Large simulation city with thousands of individuals
economy_resources: Many physical goods; labor; trade; taxation
army: City recruits feed field armies and huge battles
world_map: Regional empire map connected to city
combat: Large-scale tactical defense and campaign conquest
strengths: Exceptional scale and city-to-empire continuity
player_friction: Dense UI and simulation opacity; scale raises onboarding cost
lesson_for_our_game: Prove city-to-world continuity at tiny scale; avoid simulating thousands in slice

core_gameplay_loop: Travel; trade/quest; recruit; fight; gain renown; join or found kingdom
player_goal: Rise from adventurer to clan and realm leader
city_base: Settlement management through menus and upgrades
economy_resources: Dynamic trade goods; wages; loot; workshops; caravans
army: Persistent party with troop tiers and companions
combat: Player-led real-time battles and sieges
technology_progression: Character skills; clan tier; troop upgrades; policies
multiplayer: Separate PvP modes and dedicated servers
strengths: Personal presence makes army growth emotionally legible
player_friction: Repetition, AI/diplomacy limits and campaign/combat separation
lesson_for_our_game: Give commanders identity and persistent casualties without building an action RPG

core_gameplay_loop: Spend limited orders; develop cities; manage families; research; wage war
player_goal: Earn legitimacy/ambitions and outlast rival dynasties
city_base: Discrete cities with specialists and improvements
economy_resources: Food; iron; stone; wood; money; civics; training; orders
army: Tile units compete for shared order budget
combat: Tactical tile combat constrained by orders
technology_progression: Randomized technology choices; laws and character development
multiplayer: Hotseat, asynchronous, cloud, co-op and competitive
strengths: Shared order resource forces empire-wide priorities
player_friction: Character/event density and many yields increase cognitive load
lesson_for_our_game: A command-budget can make a small army strategically rich and multiplayer-ready

core_gameplay_loop: Harvest; build chains; manage seasons/disease; trade; defend raids; tier up
player_goal: Turn a frontier settlement into a resilient city
economy_resources: Physical goods, spoilage, farming, logistics and labor
army: Recruited/equipped guards and soldiers
world_map: Procedural local map; no grand campaign layer
combat: Optional real-time settlement defense
strengths: Detailed physical logistics and environmental specialization
player_friction: Slow early waiting and deep micromanagement can become work
lesson_for_our_game: Simulate just a few goods with clear bottleneck alerts and fast time controls

core_gameplay_loop: Collect; build; research; train; gather; march; join alliance events; fight
player_goal: Grow power and help alliance control kingdom objectives
economy_resources: Farmed map resources; currencies; speedups
army: Commander-led marches with troop tiers
world_map: Persistent shared map with free marching
combat: Real-time open-field marches, rallies and garrisons
monetization: Free-to-play in-app purchases, including acceleration/commander economy
strengths: Seamless map and social coordination create long-term attachment
player_friction: Timers, power gaps, daily chores and spend pressure can undermine fair competition
lesson_for_our_game: Keep free marching and cooperative objectives; reject paid power and punitive timers

core_gameplay_loop: Collect; upgrade base; train/compose army; attack asynchronously; join clan wars
player_goal: Improve village and win attacks/clan competitions
economy_resources: Gold; elixir; dark elixir; builders and timers
army: Pre-composed one-use deployment armies with heroes/spells
world_map: Target browser and clan war maps, not free world movement
combat: Asynchronous attack with irreversible deployment
technology_progression: Town Hall, building and troop levels
multiplayer: Clans, donations, clan wars and raids
monetization: Free-to-play with in-app purchases and optional passes
strengths: Polished short attack loop; base layout produces player expression
player_friction: Upgrade timers, progression grind and mismatch/power frustration
lesson_for_our_game: Make battles short and readable, but preserve unit command and avoid monetized waiting

core_gameplay_loop: Build; gather; train; explore; march; hunt; capture passes/behemoths with alliance
player_goal: Advance through seasonal map and alliance objectives
economy_resources: Map nodes; currencies; stamina; speedups
army: Hero-led legions with unit types and pets
world_map: Persistent seasonal shared map with terrain and portals
combat: Real-time field combat, rallies, bosses and garrisons
technology_progression: City/research tiers; heroes; artifacts; seasonal growth
strengths: Terrain, cooperative bosses and multiple legions add map tactics
player_friction: Season resets, commander investment, chores and spend gaps add friction
lesson_for_our_game: Use one cooperative world boss as a slice climax; separate strategic progression from paid stats

core_gameplay_loop: Upgrade; research; train; gather; hunt; rally; guild events; kingdom war
player_goal: Increase might and win guild/kingdom competition
economy_resources: Resources; speedups; currencies; gathering
army: Troop tiers plus heroes and rally compositions
combat: Real-time march/rally outcomes plus separate hero stages
technology_progression: Research, buildings, heroes, gear and familiars
monetization: Free-to-play with purchases and multiple subscriptions
strengths: Many social reasons to return; guild help makes progress communal
player_friction: Layered monetization, chores, protection schedules and power disparity
lesson_for_our_game: Borrow guild assistance and rally readability, not overlapping progression economies

core_gameplay_loop: Build shelter; train; research; clear PvE; collect heroes; join alliance; contest capital
player_goal: Grow settlement and alliance power through events
economy_resources: Resources; stamina; currencies; speedups
army: Troops supported by collectible heroes
combat: March/rally strategy plus small hero PvE battles
strengths: Theme, social events and varied activity feed support retention
player_friction: App-store feedback commonly cites bugs, weak story and excessive purchase pressure
lesson_for_our_game: A strong theme cannot compensate for fragmented modes; make every slice system feed the same war goal

core_gameplay_loop: Build cities; solve onboarding puzzles; train; gather; join alliance; fight on map
player_goal: Grow keep and compete in alliance/server wars
economy_resources: Resources; generals; speedups; currencies
army: Four main troop types led by generals
combat: Real-time march, rally and siege outcomes
strengths: Large-scale alliance coordination and visible marches
player_friction: Ad/gameplay mismatch complaints and strong spend/grind pressure weaken trust
lesson_for_our_game: Promise only the actual core loop; make map action playable early and progression transparent
